prose.text: ZIA has two schedule objects with nearly the same shape. Time intervals are the ones an admin creates, in [[zia.time-intervals.schema]]. The time window catalog is a second, separate list. {{catalog-endpoints}} {{read-only}}

prose.label: Terraform.
prose.text: {{tf-data-source}} The docs give other types for its outputs {{divergence:tf-data-source-types}}. {{no-managed-resource}} Whether that is intentional is open {{gap:terraform-resource-intent}}. Whether the catalog's predefined names also exist among intervals is open {{gap:predefined-intervals}}. {{tf-examples-use-time-window-catalog}} Which of the two objects the other rule types' `timeWindows` entry accepts is open {{gap:rule-field-references}}; see [[zia.time-intervals.rule-usage]].

checks.do: Whether the catalog's predefined names, such as Work hours, appear in a live list of intervals.

catalog-endpoints.statement: `GET /timeWindows` and `GET /timeWindows/lite` list the time intervals used by the Firewall policy or the URL Filtering policy; they are separate from `/timeIntervals`.

expect.operationId: Time Window Resource Get Time Windows
Time Interval Resource Get Time Interval

read-only.statement: The time window catalog is read-only in the API specification: both paths expose only GET.
read-only.conditions: Absence of any other method on the two paths in the captured OpenAPI document.

day-key-singular.statement: A time window names its days in `dayOfWeek` (singular), where a time interval uses `daysOfWeek`; the other four fields match.

tf-data-source.statement: The Terraform provider exposes the catalog as the data source `zia_firewall_filtering_time_window`, looked up by `id` or `name` (documented examples: Work hours, Weekends, Off hours). Its schema returns `start_time` and `end_time` as integers and `day_of_week` as a list of strings.

quotes: "id": { Type: schema.TypeInt, Computed: true, Optional: true, },

tf-data-source.conditions: Statement changed from "returning start_time, end_time and day_of_week as strings": that is the docs; the schema types the times as TypeInt and day_of_week as a list of strings, so the claim now states the schema and the docs' types are the tf-data-source-types divergence. Lookup by id added from the schema.

no-managed-resource.statement: The Terraform provider has no managed resource or data source for user-created time intervals; only the time window data source exists in the documentation.
no-managed-resource.conditions: Absence: the provider docs directories at the pin contain no time interval resource or data source page.

tf-examples-use-time-window-catalog.statement: In the Terraform provider's examples, the Firewall Filtering, Firewall DNS, Firewall IPS, Forwarding Control and Traffic Capture rules fill their time windows with the id of the `zia_firewall_filtering_time_window` data source.

terraform-resource-intent.title: Whether a Terraform time interval resource is planned or deliberately excluded
terraform-resource-intent.detail: The provider has no resource for `/timeIntervals`; whether that is planned, excluded on purpose, or available only through the API and SDKs is not stated in the provider source. The provider changelog or issue tracker may say.

predefined-intervals.title: Whether predefined objects such as Work hours also exist in /timeIntervals
predefined-intervals.detail: The Terraform data source documents Work hours, Weekends and Off hours as names in the time window catalog. Whether the same predefined objects also appear in the `/timeIntervals` list, or that endpoint is entirely user-managed, is not shown. A list on a clean tenant answers it.

rule-field-references.title: Which object a rule's timeWindows entry references: an interval or a window
rule-field-references.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the shared `timeWindows` field "accepts a list of {id, name} references to either Time Interval or Firewall Time Window objects depending on the rule type". The Terraform examples show which catalog five rule types use (claim tf-examples-use-time-window-catalog); for URL Filtering, SSL Inspection, Cloud App Control, DLP, File Type Control, Bandwidth Control and the other rule types no source says which catalog supplies the ID.

tf-data-source-types.summary: The time window data source docs type start_time, end_time and day_of_week as strings and name as required; the schema types the times as integers, day_of_week as a list of strings, and name as optional.

positions.says: The docs list name as required and start_time, end_time and day_of_week as strings.

quotes: * `name` - (Required) The name of the time window to be exported.

positions.says: The schema declares name optional, start_time and end_time as TypeInt, and day_of_week as a list of strings.

tf-data-source-types.impact: Expressions that treat day_of_week as one string (for example string functions on it) fail type checks, and start_time and end_time come back as numbers; write configurations against the schema types.
